# exe: /home/ubuntu/.local/bin/porter
# args: 
With Porter you can package your application artifact, client tools, configuration and deployment logic together as a versioned bundle that you can distribute, and then install with a single command.

Most commands require a Docker daemon, either local or remote.

Try our QuickStart https://porter.sh/quickstart to learn how to use Porter.

Usage:
  porter [flags]
  porter [command]

Examples:
  porter create
  porter build
  porter install
  porter uninstall

Resources:
  bundles       Bundle commands
  credentials   Credentials commands
  installations Installation commands
  mixins        Mixin commands. Mixins assist with authoring bundles.
  parameters    Parameter set commands
  plugins       Plugin commands. Plugins enable Porter to work on different cloud providers and systems.
  storage       Manage data stored by Porter

Commands:
  mcp           Start an MCP server over stdio

Aliased Commands:
  archive       Archive a bundle from a reference
  build         Build a bundle
  copy          Copy a bundle
  create        Create a bundle
  explain       Explain a bundle
  inspect       Inspect a bundle
  install       Create a new installation of a bundle
  invoke        Invoke a custom action on an installation
  lint          Lint a bundle
  list          List installed bundles
  logs          Show the logs from an installation
  publish       Publish a bundle
  show          Show an installation of a bundle
  uninstall     Uninstall an installation
  upgrade       Upgrade an installation

Meta Commands:
  completion    Generate completion script
  config        Config commands
  schema        Print the JSON schema for the Porter manifest
  version       Print the application version

Flags:
      --context string         Name of the configuration context to use. When unset, Porter uses the current-context from the config file, falling back to the context named "default".
      --experimental strings   Comma separated list of experimental features to enable. See https://porter.sh/configuration/#experimental-feature-flags for available feature flags.
  -h, --help                   help for porter
      --verbosity string       Threshold for printing messages to the console. Available values are: debug, info, warning, error. (default "info")
  -v, --version                Print the application version

Use "porter [command] --help" for more information about a command.
